retained_foundations: For the generic arithmetic count, the product of the eligible primitive parts must satisfy the logarithmic size inequality in PropGK uniformly in the twist, field of the character kernel and level. ETS9–11 give pointwise finiteness, an integer independent of the later coefficient data, its exact minimal valuations, and the local restrictions at every eligible prime. ETS12–14 resolve the stated vanishing and bounded-parameter cases.

On the linked ordinary-family route match the prime-to-order arithmetic seed and the rank-two CM twist to the integral Hecke support. The required supported primes below the characteristic-prime curves, the ensuing exceptional transfers and classicality must yield the weight-zero and both-rank statements at one mark. See ETS4–6 and the comparison with the pinned Brox reconstruction.

On the simultaneous windows the direct height reduction of ETS24 still requires a uniform bound for the logarithms of the residual odd K-group orders on the base and cyclic subextensions, as conductor and twist grow. The complete dyadic, odd-minus and listed base-invariant contributions have the stated bounds.

formal_consumer.scope: The strict groups are finite. On the original cohomological window the complete dyadic term and one odd sign are bounded. The other odd orders reduce to a base term and primitive ratios on cyclic subextensions. At the split rank-three triple the central strict tangent term also has a uniform bound. The adjacent terms carry both signs; normalized polarized triangular families can still contain the level-two even cyclotomic eigenspace. The uniform estimate on the remaining orders or a proof through ordinary automorphic support is still needed. For mixed adjacent signs the global cup obstruction lies in a finite negative localization kernel. Its whole order is bounded independently of auxiliary places and coefficient depth.
